data.cultural_impact: The name Arel holds a deep cultural impact as it is rooted in ancient Greek mythology. Ares, the Greek god of war, was associated with strength, courage, and power. These qualities are highly valued in various cultures, especially in warrior societies. Thus, the name Arel, reflecting its Greek origin, evokes images of bravery and strength. Moreover, given the historical Christian resistance against pagan influences, the reinterpretation of the god's name into a Christ-centered identity further strengthens its cultural significance within the faith.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Arel holds spiritual significance as a symbol of steadfast spirit and courageous faith. In the Bible, we find numerous references to lions and eagles, animals that embody the characteristics of Ares. For instance, David, the future king of Israel, lamented despairingly that he was a man "who craves to be among the dead like those lying in the grave, like the dust that the wind has blown away from the face of the earth" (Psalm 22:15). Overhearing his words, the LORD answered him, "I myself will be with you; I will save you and deliver you from the hand of the Philistines. And I will bring you back from the captivity of the Philistines and will make you renowned more than all the nations, and you shall know that I am the LORD, who rescues you, O Jerusalem" (Jeremiah 30:11) - symbolized by the lion's roar. The eagle, in its turn, was a reflection of God's divine protection, guidance, andhead, "But they who wait for the LORD shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles; they shall run and not be weary; they shall walk and not faint" (Isaiah 40:31).
